citation_or_source: PDB 9C59 (cryo-EM 4.3 A; Begley, Aragon & Baker 2024, PMID 39705307); coordinates measured in this job
claim_tested: Residues 1-14 of AP3D1 form a discrete helix separate from the alpha-solenoid trunk
key_finding: CA(i)-CA(i+4) 5.96-6.63 A over residues 1-15, then 7.91/9.83/13.31/11.35 A at residues 12-15, then 5.07-6.23 A from residue 16. Two distinct helices.
organism_assay_context: Human AP-3 core on a lipid nanodisc with myr-Arf1 and LAMP1 cargo
limitations: Measurement is of a deposited model, not of density directly; 4.3 A resolution

citation_or_source: PDB 9C5C, 9C58, 9RTW; modelled residue ranges read from mmCIF in this job
claim_tested: The AP3D1 N-terminal helix is a stable, ordered element of the AP-3 core
key_finding: Delta residues 1-17 are not modelled in 9C5C (apo), 9C58 (AP-3 + myr-Arf1) or 9RTW (AP-3 on tubular membranes). Delta starts at residue 18 in all three.
limitations: Absence of density is evidence of flexibility, not of absence of the segment

citation_or_source: PDB 9C59 / 9C5B; distances and B-factors measured in this job
claim_tested: The AP3D1 N-terminal helix contacts the bilayer in the membrane-bound AP-3 structure
key_finding: Minimum heavy-atom distance from delta 1-14 to the Arf1 myristoylated helix is 31.9 A (mean 55.0 A); to LAMP1 cargo 31.4 A. Mean B-factor 266.8 for residues 1-17 versus 183.2 for 18-60. Relative solvent accessibility 0.24-0.84 across 1-17, identical in the isolated chain and the whole complex.
organism_assay_context: Human AP-3 dimer on a lipid nanodisc
limitations: No lipids are modelled (HETATM contains only GTP and Mg), so the bilayer position is inferred from the Arf1 anchor. A direct plane fit was attempted and rejected as geometrically degenerate.

citation_or_source: AlphaFold DB AF-O14617-F1 v6, downloaded and parsed in this job; method PMID 34265844
claim_tested: The AP3D1 N-terminal helix is a conditionally folding segment
key_finding: Mean pLDDT 48.3 for residues 1-14 versus 91.3 for residues 18-60 and 90.5 for 18-600. CA(i)-CA(i+4) reproduces the same helix break at residues 12-15.
limitations: Low pLDDT indicates disorder or conditional folding, and does not by itself demonstrate membrane binding

citation_or_source: Computed in this job from UniProt sequences; Eisenberg consensus scale
claim_tested: The N-terminal amphipathic helix is specific to the delta subunit among adaptin large subunits
key_finding: Hydrophobic moment of the first 24 residues: AP3D1 0.421, AP1G1 0.273, AP4E1 0.234, AP2A1 0.197, AP3B1 0.192, AP2B1 0.079. AP3D1 1-14 reaches 0.464. The delta value is 1.5x to 5.3x the paralog values.
limitations: Hydrophobic moment is a sequence statistic with no direct energetic meaning

citation_or_source: Computed in this job; null = 20,396 reviewed human UniProt proteins
claim_tested: A high N-terminal hydrophobic moment identifies a membrane-inserting helix
key_finding: AP3D1 first 24 aa muH 0.421 = 98.0th percentile (P = 0.020), first 14 aa 0.464 = 94.6th percentile (P = 0.054). The ApoA-I class A surface-binding control reaches the 97.9th percentile and the deep inserter Sar1A only the 91.6th. The metric does not separate the two classes.
limitations: Null uses N-terminal windows only, so it is not a null over all internal helices

citation_or_source: Computed in this job; Wimley-White interfacial scale
claim_tested: The hydrophobic face predicts deep, curvature-generating insertion
key_finding: Face transfer free energy per face residue: Sar1A -0.543, ArfGAP1 ALPS1 -0.385, AP3D1 1-14 -0.266, Arf1 1-17 -0.214, epsin1 H0 -0.078, ApoA-I +0.033. Totals: AP3D1 1-14 -1.86 kcal/mol over 7 face residues versus ALPS1 -4.23 over 11 and Sar1A -6.52 over 12.
limitations: Interfacial scale models partitioning to a neutral bilayer interface and ignores electrostatics, helix dipole and lipid composition

citation_or_source: Computed in this job; helical-wheel geometry at 100 deg/residue
claim_tested: The helix architecture resembles an inserting helix rather than the class A surface-binding architecture
key_finding: Apolar arc: AP3D1 1-14 220 deg, epsin1 H0 220 deg, Sar1A 240 deg, ArfGAP1 ALPS1 200 deg, ApoA-I class A 100 deg. Mean absolute angle of Lys/Arg from the moment vector: AP3D1 123.9 deg, epsin1 H0 132.5 deg, ApoA-I 101.1 deg.
limitations: Arc width is a coarse descriptor; several published inserting helices (amphiphysin H0, 340 deg) fall outside the AP3D1 range

citation_or_source: Computed in this job from UniProt orthologue sequences
claim_tested: The N-terminal amphipathic helix is conserved across the whole AP-3 delta family
key_finding: Residues 1-24 are identical in human, mouse and chicken delta, retain the MAL[KR].[VK]K pattern in Drosophila (MALKKVKGNFFERMF, muH 0.280) and C. elegans (MALRKVRSNIDRIF), and are unrecognisable in S. cerevisiae Apl5 (MTSLYAPGAEDIRQRLRPFGFFFE, muH 0.350, net charge 0, apolar arc 300 deg). The adjacent trunk helix is conserved.
organism_assay_context: Vertebrate, insect, nematode and yeast orthologues
limitations: Apl5 is a divergent orthologue overall, so lack of conservation at the N-terminus is not specific evidence against function

citation_or_source: PDB 7P3X; modelled range read in this job
claim_tested: Yeast AP-3 resolves a delta N-terminal helix
key_finding: Yeast Apl5 is modelled from residue 63 onward, so the N-terminal region is unresolved and the question is untested in yeast.
limitations: Homology model fitted into a low-resolution map

claim_tested: Membrane recruitment of AP-3 requires an N-terminal delta amphipathic helix
key_finding: The published mechanism attributes recruitment to two Arf1 binding sites: the first flexibly tethers AP-3 to the membrane, cargo binding rigidifies the complex, and a second Arf1 templates dimerisation. No delta N-terminal helix is proposed as a membrane anchor.
organism_assay_context: Reconstituted human AP-3 on lipid nanodiscs
limitations: The reconstituted core may omit elements present in the full complex in cells

claim_tested: AP-3 membrane recruitment depends on a delta amphipathic helix
key_finding: AP-3 membrane association in vitro is increased by GTP-gamma-S, inhibited by brefeldin A and promoted by recombinant myristoylated ARF1; lowering ARF1-GTP redistributes AP-3 to the cytosol.
organism_assay_context: Rat liver membranes and cultured cells
limitations: Does not test the delta N-terminus directly

claim_tested: The delta N-terminus controls AP-3 membrane recruitment
key_finding: The delta ear domain binds sigma3 and this interdomain interaction inhibits AP-3 recruitment to membranes in vitro and in vivo by interfering with Arf binding. Regulation maps to the delta C-terminal ear, not the N-terminus.
limitations: Does not exclude an additional N-terminal contribution

citation_or_source: Literature search in this job (PubMed, 4 query formulations)
claim_tested: Some primary study has tested the AP3D1 N-terminal helix for membrane binding
key_finding: No primary study was found that deletes, mutates or assays AP3D1 residues 1-17 for liposome binding, insertion or curvature generation. The hypothesis is untested rather than contradicted.
limitations: Absence in PubMed searches is not proof that no such experiment exists

citation_or_source: UniProt REST; 180 vertebrate species retrieved and scored in this job
claim_tested: The AP3D1 N-terminal segment is a functionally constrained element
key_finding: Residues 1-14 identical to human MALKMVKGSIDRMF in 123/180 species and physicochemically identical in 168/180. Per-position identity 92.2-100 percent except M5 at 68.3 percent, where the variant is the conservative M5I in 45 teleosts. Twelve outliers are unreviewed gene models with truncated start sites.
organism_assay_context: Teleosts to mammals, roughly 450 Myr of divergence
limitations: Constraint shows the sequence matters and does not identify the mechanism; the apolar face and the polar side are conserved to the same degree

citation_or_source: UniProt O14617 JSON and five isoform FASTAs retrieved in this job
claim_tested: A residue-numbered annotation on AP3D1 1-14 is isoform safe
key_finding: All five annotated isoforms (O14617-1 to O14617-5) begin MALKMVKGSIDRMFDKNLQDLVRG. The five alternative-sequence features span residues 117-285, 168-258, 746-877 and 866-866, none touching residues 1-24.
limitations: UniProt isoform annotation may not cover every expressed transcript
